transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Carl. What's the issue today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Carl. I've been experiencing terrible packet loss and latency spikes on my broadband connection for the last four days, and it's making my competitive gaming and streaming completely unplayable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we look into line statistics, I need to complete security verification. What is your full name and account address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dominic Vance, 12 St Mary's Road, Sheffield, S2 4BF.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the security question answer for the name of your first school, Dominic?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Bramall Primary.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Now, what kind of speeds and ping times are you seeing during these gaming sessions?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My base ping to UK servers is usually twelve milliseconds, but every few minutes it spikes to over four hundred milliseconds with fifteen to twenty percent packet loss.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you connected using a wired Ethernet cable or over Wi-Fi?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's a direct Cat 6 Ethernet cable straight into port 1 of the Hub 5 router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you tried restarting the Hub 5 router recently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I powered it off for ten minutes yesterday, and the issue came right back as soon as it re-synced.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you check whether there are any firmware updates pending for the Hub 5 router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Your app says the router is on the latest release.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your Hub 5 is currently running firmware version 3.14.8, which is the latest stable release deployed nationwide.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is IPv6 enabled on the WAN interface, or are we on dual-stack?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your connection is running native dual-stack with an assigned slash fifty-six IPv6 delegation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Have you seen any issues with IPv6 neighbor discovery flapping on that switch?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, the NDP table has zero reported errors over the trailing forty-eight hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What about MTU size? Is it set to standard fifteen hundred or fourteen ninety-two?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: PPPoE overhead sets the WAN MTU to fourteen ninety-two automatically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I see. And what does the packet loss counter show on the downstream port?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Downstream interface has logged zero dropped frames across all four gigabit LAN ports.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, which proves the issue is upstream congestion outside the home network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not necessarily. Internal device processes can generate socket timeouts independent of port status.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll run a background optical line test to our terminal to inspect packet error rates. Bear with me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Dominic. The physical line sync is rock solid at nine hundred megabits down and one hundred up, with zero CRC errors on the physical layer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The raw sync speed isn't the problem, Carl! It's latency jitter and upstream bufferbloat! I ran an MTR traceroute and hop three inside your core network is dropping packets! This has been going on for four days and nobody is fixing it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our core network does not have bufferbloat. Consumer traceroutes are notoriously misleading because routers deprioritize ICMP ping packets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's not just ICMP! UDP game packets in Counter-Strike and Discord voice chat are literally rubber-banding every thirty seconds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As I said, if the physical layer shows zero packet loss at the ONT, the line test registers as healthy.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then explain why four other people on my street using S-Net have reported the exact same packet loss on the Sheffield local forum since Tuesday!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously I cannot comment on unverified gossip on public internet forums.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's not gossip, it's your routing gateway! Can you at least escalate a ticket to your Level 2 network operations team to inspect the node load?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I take full responsibility for network escalations, and I will check the node utilization metrics in our regional telemetry portal. Bear with me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for holding, Dominic. I am looking at the node telemetry for the Sheffield South aggregation switch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what does the upstream interface graph show?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Upstream bandwidth utilization peaked at seventy-eight percent at eight PM yesterday, which is within operational tolerance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Seventy-eight percent on a shared GPON segment is causing queue latency spikes! That's exactly when my games start hitching! This service is utterly useless!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm the hardware connection before I consider raising an incident, you are using Cat 6 Ethernet into port 1 on the Hub 5, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! I told you that fifteen minutes ago! Cat 6 direct to port 1, brand new cable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, seventy-eight percent utilization does not warrant a tier-three network dispatch under our SLA thresholds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So you're just refusing to fix a congested gateway that I'm paying sixty quid a month for?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm telling you what the diagnostic platform shows. There is no line fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is absolute incompetence. You have no idea how network routing works!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Only an idiot would blame our core gateway when you're probably running torrents or background updates on your PC!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did you just call me an idiot? I am a senior systems engineer! I want your manager right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am not transferring you to a manager when you called up shouting about ping times.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am filing an official complaint with Ofcom and the telecommunications ombudsman today!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are free to file whatever complaint you like, Dominic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Give me your employee ID number immediately!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: My operative ID is 4491. I will log this ticket under your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And is this packet loss going to be resolved, or am I leaving this call with a broken connection?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As the line passes all automated hardware health tests, no engineering visit will be scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unbelievable. I'm cancelling my contract for breach of service.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can discuss cancellation penalties with our customer relations team during weekday hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will be doing exactly that. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, goodbye.
